title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

errors: The equivalence (d)⇒(a) is not proved on this page. It relies on earlier axioms (At 1–At 7) not visible here, notably the link between x ≤ Y, the boundary, and ≪. As stated it is plausible but depends on those axioms.

Grothendieck writes ∂X as a Sup for ≤ and then equates omb(∂X) with the union of the omb(Y). That requires omb to send this Sup to a union, i.e. a point under the sup lies under some Y. This must come from an earlier axiom; it is not automatic in a general poset.

ideas.what: Axiom At 8: each piece X has a point lying under X but not under its combinatorial boundary ∂X, i.e. the 'open cell' omb(X)° is nonempty.
ideas.modern_name: Nonempty open cells / every stratum is detected by a point (as in regular CW complexes and cell posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical cell-complex theory (Whitehead); poset formulations by Björner (CW posets, 1984)
ideas.where_published: Only in the 1986 'Analysis situs' manuscripts; the Esquisse d'un Programme only announces a tame topology programme

ideas.what: Corollary: X ≤ Y ⇔ omb(X) ⊂ omb(Y) ⇔ omb(X)° ⊂ omb(Y) ⇔ omb(X)° ∩ omb(Y) ≠ ∅.
ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition for stratifications / face-poset characterization of incidence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney / Thom–Mather stratification theory (frontier condition); Björner for posets

ideas.what: Multiombre: representing an abstract figure by the family of shadows of its pieces, giving a bijection of subfigures (1.53).
ideas.modern_name: Set-theoretic (point-set) realization of an abstract cell poset; Birkhoff-type representation via down-sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (representation of distributive lattices); Stone; combinatorial topology folklore

missed.claim: The page is part of an unpublished axiomatic 'atelier' framework (At 1–At 8, relations ≤ and ≪, lieux, ombres, multiombres) for a combinatorial/tame analysis situs. It can be read as a sketch of Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' at the level of abstract incidence structures. The specific statement here (nonempty open cells ⇒ the frontier condition ⇒ faithful set-theoretic realization) is standard. The overall axiomatic framework, however, has not been developed or published.
missed.quote: At 8 Soit X ∈ 𝓜, et soit ∂X = Sup Y ... Alors ∃ x ∈ L tel que x ≤ X, x ≰ ∂X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with modern poset-stratified spaces (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka), cellular sheaves (Curry) and finite-space models (Barmak–Minian). It is mainly of historical interest as Grothendieck's own route to tame topology.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is the standard frontier condition and nonempty-open-cell axiom, recast in Grothendieck's private vocabulary. Only the existence and detail of the unpublished axiomatic framework is of historical note.
